summary:
With the season just about to kick off, there's not much competitive action to discuss yet, but plenty of pre-season activity and squad building is underway across the division.

Eccleshall have been particularly quiet on the pitch but extremely busy off it, securing a string of key player retentions including captain Nicky Parker and vice-captains Levi Hunter and Adam Whitehouse. They've also brought in Max Chimenes on dual registration from Stafford Rangers and promoted Will Silvester from the reserves. This suggests a club confident in their setup and focused on continuity after finishing second last season.

Stafford Town appear well organized heading into the campaign, running a coordinated player sponsorship drive that's been announced regularly alongside team news. They've signed Dan Clarkson on dual registration from Chasetown and promoted two development players, Luke Crowther and Jacob Kennett, to first team forms. Their recent pre-season friendly against Cradley Town finished 6-3, suggesting good attacking form, though that's a friendly result so worth taking with a pinch of salt.

New Mills seem to be taking a more community-focused approach, running a crossbar competition at half time for home games and releasing detailed printed programmes. They've also been consistent with fixture announcements and seem well organized, though they did lose 2-0 to FC Trafford in a pre-season friendly.

Telford Town have been notably busy in the transfer market, announcing four signings in a single day (Ibrahim Almane, Joe Danby, Desean Martin, and Ofori), suggesting manager Shaun Ralph is making significant changes to the squad. They drew 2-2 with Stourport Swifts in their most recent friendly.

Among the new teams coming up, Crewe FC have made history as the club's first ever entry into the National League System, and they've been building their squad deliberately. Dawley Town are also newcomers to the division and will be keen to make an impression in their opening game.

Allscott Heath have been particularly active in the last few days, announcing multiple signings including returnees George Cross (who scored 15 goals in the Shropshire Premier Division last season), Harry Morris, Kian Garbett, and several others. They've clearly pursued a strategy of bringing back trusted players with recent successful seasons at lower levels.

Foley Meir have done significant squad building work, announcing new signings including Jake Walklett from Rocester, Connor Lawton from Market Drayton, and Tyler Mistry from Macclesfield, while also retaining experienced players like Marc Grocott as player-coach. They seem focused on adding quality depth.

AFC Bridgnorth have been methodical with their retentions and signings, confirming their management team and securing their top goalscorer from last season, Suar Dedja, along with several new additions including Mason Straker from Stourport and goalkeeper Jack Breckell.

Cheadle Heath Nomads finished their pre-season strongly with a convincing 4-0 win over FC United Manchester U21, suggesting decent attacking form heading into their season opener.

Sandbach themselves appear to have had a quiet pre-season by comparison, with their focus on season ticket offers and promotion rather than extensive squad announcements, which might suggest confidence in existing personnel.
